content_voiceover: This is the ASC4FIRST trial design, evaluating asciminib versus imatinib or a second generation TKI as first line therapy for chronic myeloid leukemia, a new indication marked here as a new adaptation. Four hundred five newly diagnosed, Philadelphia chromosome positive, chronic phase patients with no prior TKI exposure were enrolled. Before randomization, the treating physician and patient selected which TKI the patient would receive if assigned to the investigator selected arm, either imatinib or a second generation agent. Patients were then stratified by that preselected TKI and by ELTS risk category, low, intermediate, or high, and randomized one to one. Two hundred one patients received asciminib eighty milligrams once daily, split into an imatinib stratum and a second generation TKI stratum, while two hundred four received their investigator selected TKI at label doses. The primary endpoints were major molecular response at week forty eight, both overall, asciminib versus all investigator selected TKIs, and specifically within the imatinib stratum. Key secondary endpoints repeated these comparisons at week ninety six.
keypoints: Four hundred five newly diagnosed CML chronic phase patients, TKI naive
Randomized one to one: asciminib versus investigator selected imatinib or 2G TKI
Stratified by preselected TKI and ELTS risk category
Primary endpoint: MMR at week 48, overall and in the imatinib stratum
keypoint_voiceover: ASC4FIRST is a first line trial testing whether asciminib beats standard TKIs, including imatinib, in treatment naive CML. The key design feature is the prerandomization TKI selection, which lets the trial compare asciminib against imatinib specifically as well as against all investigator selected TKIs. Major molecular response at week 48 was the primary endpoint, with week 96 as a durability check.
